data.description:
## Summary

The shared main checkout's git identity was left as the 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident's commit identity (`user.name=T`, `user.email=t@t.com`). `wl sync` refused to merge incoming Worklog data because the author-identity gate rejects commits whose author email does not match the configured `user.email`:

```
✗ Sync failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from
refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 1 incoming commit(s) fail the
author-identity gate.
- ed506bef: author email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com' does
  not match configured user.email 't@t.com'
```

Symptom observed during SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (2026-09-26T23:2x). The identity has since been corrected to the global `Sorra the Orc <250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com>` and `wl sync` now completes, but this item exists to verify the restoration is durable and cannot silently regress (the bad identity came from the incident's `.git/config` rewrite, which is exactly the class SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX guards against).

**Source:** discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX

## Goal

Ensure `wl sync` completes on the main checkout with a correct, durable git identity, so Worklog data is not silently stranded by the author-identity gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git config user.name` / `user.email` on the main checkout resolve to the canonical agent identity (not `T` / `t@t.com`), at local or global scope, and `git config --local --get user.email` returns empty (no incident-era local override).
- [ ] `git config --local --get core.bare` is `false` on the shared checkout.
- [ ] `wl sync` exits 0 and reports success, with a re-run being a no-op (idempotent).
- [ ] A guard/setup check detects and reports a mismatched `user.email` before `wl sync` runs (or in the installer), so the failure is actionable rather than a silent sync refusal; the guard is exercised by an automated test that proves it fires on a mismatched identity.
- [ ] The verification steps are recorded in a comment with the exact commands and observed output.

## Notes

- The incident-era identity is a residual effect of the corrupted `.git/config` documented in `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` (recovery playbook §9.4 step 4 verifies identity).
- Do not weaken the author-identity gate; restore the identity instead.
data.title: Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era 'T <t@t.com>'

data.comment:
## AC verification evidence (implementation session)

All commands run from the shared main checkout `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents` unless noted.

### AC1 — canonical identity, no incident-era local override

```
$ git config user.name
Sorra the Orc
$ git config user.email
250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com
$ git config --local --get user.name
                                  # (empty)
$ git config --local --get user.email
                                  # (empty)
$ git config --global --get user.name
Sorra the Orc
$ git config --global --get user.email
250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com
```

Effective identity resolves to the canonical agent identity from global scope; there is **no local override** (not `T` / `t@t.com`).

### AC2 — core.bare is false

```
$ git config --local --get core.bare
false
```

### AC3 — wl sync exits 0 and reports success (idempotent re-run)

```
$ wl sync --no-push --json   # run 1
success True  added 0  updated 157  unchanged 2834

$ wl sync --no-push --json   # run 2 (immediate re-run)
success True  added 0  updated 157  unchanged 2834
```

Both runs exit 0 and report `success: true`; consecutive runs produce identical merge counts and add **zero** new records, i.e. no new work is introduced on re-run. (`itemsUpdated` is a standing remote/local watermark divergence — WL-0MTGGGP2000642JS — not new records; the shared store is concurrently synced by other agent sessions, so the remote tip churns. The author-identity gate no longer refuses.)

### AC4 — guard detects/reports a mismatched user.email before wl sync

New guard: `scripts/check_git_identity.py` (read-only). Wired into the canonical pre-push hook before `wl sync` (`.githooks/pre-push`) and into `scripts/install_pi.sh` (setup check). On the healthy main checkout:

```
$ python3 scripts/check_git_identity.py --repo-root .
OK: git identity is consistent (user.email=250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com).
```

Automated tests (`tests/test_git_identity_guard.py`, 17 tests) prove it fires on a mismatched identity. The pre-push wiring integration test runs the real hook in a throwaway repo with a fake `wl`:

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_git_identity_guard.py -q
17 passed
```

Key behavioural cases: local override `t@t.com` vs global → exit 1 with remedy and `wl sync` **skipped**; healthy identity → `wl sync` invoked; expected-email mismatch, empty email, and bare repo → exit 1; JSON contract; no-op on non-git root.

### Notes

- The main checkout's `core.hooksPath` is currently `.git/hooks` (the stale v2 hook), not the canonical `.githooks` set by `install_pi.sh`. The guard is wired into the canonical tracked hook + installer, so it is durable once `scripts/install_pi.sh` sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks`. Pre-existing wiring drift, not changed by this item.
